title: OpenAI public plugin package
objective: Make Qdral SOFTWARE_READY and SUBMISSION_READY for the current OpenAI Plugins Directory without widening Qdral authority: package the existing public Streamable HTTP MCP path using the current portable plugin format, derive OpenAI-facing tool/auth metadata from Qdral's authoritative contracts, prepare domain-verification and review evidence, and keep SUBMITTED, APPROVED, PUBLISHED, and ACCOUNT_VERIFIED as externally observed states that cannot be inferred from software completion.

include: a portable plugin package rooted in current plugin.json plus the current MCP package configuration for exactly one Qdral remote MCP connection, with OpenAI-specific settings confined to the documented OpenAI extension namespace where required
production-configuration support for the existing public HTTPS Streamable HTTP MCP relay endpoint without adding a generic proxy or second authorization path

current OAuth 2.1 protected-resource metadata and per-tool securitySchemes derived from the authoritative Qdral OAuth/tool contract, including exact tool names, descriptions, schemas, annotations, scopes, local-only exclusions, and default-deny behavior

a configurable /.well-known/openai-apps-challenge domain-verification response path or deployment artifact that cannot grant workspace trust, approval, executable admission, device enrollment, or remote-session authority
accurate plugin metadata and configurable HTTPS website, support, privacy, terms, and security-reporting URLs with validation that package artifacts contain no credentials or private keys

a submission/review evidence bundle containing exactly five positive test cases, exactly three negative test cases, release notes, a demo-recording evidence slot, tool-scan/verifier output, and explicit external prerequisite/blocker recording
an explicit distribution state machine preserving SOFTWARE_READY, SUBMISSION_READY, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, PUBLISHED, and ACCOUNT_VERIFIED as distinct states with no automatic promotion

regression tests proving the OpenAI package is generated or checked against the canonical tool contract and OAuth matrix, exposes no local-only tools, contains no secrets, and adds no kernel, approval, trust, lease, executable, process, browser, desktop-input, clipboard, or generic-network authority
re-verification of current official OpenAI plugin documentation before closeout because provider packaging, review, verification, and directory requirements may change independently of Qdral
exclude: claiming or performing provider submission, approval, publication, or account availability without directly observed external evidence and any required owner action
embedding OpenAI API keys, OAuth client secrets, relay private keys, access tokens, refresh tokens, credentials, or other secrets in the plugin package or review bundle

purchasing paid hosting, a paid custom domain, a paid certificate, or another paid publication prerequisite; unavoidable external cost is recorded as a publication blocker under the zero-founder-cost rule

adding or widening any kernel capability, MCP tool, OAuth scope, profile, approval class, workspace trust right, executable-admission right, remote-session lease right, browser/desktop actuation, shell/interpreter, or generic socket/proxy authority
provider-specific execution logic that bypasses the provider-neutral MCP builder, qdrald policy kernel, existing relay authorization, or existing tool contract
activating SG-000068 or any P18 grain before this grain closes canonically

authority_delta.network: None; this grain packages/configures the already-authorized public relay path and may add only a bounded verification response that grants no agent authority.
authority_delta.secrets: None; package and review artifacts must be secret-free.

invariants: plugin discovery, tool scanning, directory review, or provider metadata never constitutes authorization; qdrald, OAuth ceilings, device binding, remote-session lease, workspace trust, and approval remain authoritative
OpenAI-facing tool metadata is derived from or mechanically checked against the canonical Qdral tool contract and cannot silently expose local-only or denied tools
no software or CI result may promote the provider distribution state to SUBMITTED, APPROVED, PUBLISHED, or ACCOUNT_VERIFIED without directly observed external evidence
the package, fixtures, logs, screenshots, demo evidence, and release artifacts contain no Qdral, OpenAI, OAuth, relay, device, or user secret
provider requirement drift is checked against current official OpenAI documentation immediately before closeout; stale packaging or review assumptions fail closed
P18 remains inactive and no computer-use authority is introduced by public distribution work

acceptance.claim: A reproducible current-format OpenAI plugin package validates from clean source and contains the required portable plugin/MCP metadata, accurate product metadata, configurable legal/support/security URLs, and no secret material.

Every OpenAI-visible tool name, description, input/output schema, annotation, securityScheme, OAuth scope, and profile membership is derived from or mechanically checked against the authoritative Qdral tool/OAuth contracts; local-only and denied tools remain undiscoverable and unauthorized.

The existing public HTTPS Streamable HTTP MCP path passes an OpenAI-compatible qualification fixture including protected-resource/OAuth metadata, exact resource binding, tool discovery/call behavior, domain-verification challenge behavior, and fail-closed negative cases without adding a second authorization path.

The submission-review bundle contains exactly five positive and three negative provider-review test cases, release notes, demo-recording evidence slot, current tool-scan/verifier evidence, legal/support/security URL evidence, and explicit external prerequisites/blockers, with SOFTWARE_READY and SUBMISSION_READY separated from all provider-controlled states.

Zero-cost and authority-boundary regressions prove no paid service is made mandatory, no secret enters package/review artifacts, no provider-specific path bypasses qdrald or the canonical MCP builder, no authority widens, and SG-000068 plus SG-000073 through SG-000086 remain inactive.

Exact-head CI, genuine TypeSafe Jev, Alibaba Open Code Review, manual review of excluded files, current official OpenAI requirement re-verification, release qualification, and zero unresolved review threads all pass.

external_requirements_verified.source_policy: Official OpenAI documentation must be re-checked before closeout; these URLs are planning evidence, not a promise that provider rules remain unchanged.

successor_requirements.sg_000068: The next COTRA-P17 provider/distribution grain may activate only after SG-000067 closes canonically.
successor_requirements.p18: SG-000073 through SG-000086 remain new-grain-only and may not activate during SG-000067.

done_when: Qdral has one exact, tested, secret-free, current-format OpenAI plugin package and review bundle that is SOFTWARE_READY and SUBMISSION_READY over the existing governed relay/MCP authority, while every provider-controlled publication state remains explicit external evidence rather than a software claim.
